 Notes to the Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for the three and nine month period ended September 30, 2026 
 Note 1 Corporate information Klarna Group plc is a public company with limited liability incorporated under the laws of England and Wales. The interim consolidated financial statements consist of Klarna Group plc and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (collectively, “Klarna,” the “Company,” the “Group,” “we,” “us,” or “our”). Klarna is a global digital bank and technology-driven flexible payments provider, with operations spanning multiple countries. We connect consumers and merchants with comprehensive payment solutions and tailored advertising solutions, both online and offline. Our payment solutions provide consumers with more control and flexibility over their payments. The Company's ordinary shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange following the completion of the Company's initial public offering on September 10, 2025. Note 2 Accounting principles 1. Basis of preparation and consolidation The interim condensed consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with IAS 34, Interim Financial Reporting, as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (“IASB”) and have been prepared on a historical cost basis, except for equity investments, derivatives and consumer receivables at fair value through profit or loss or at fair value through other comprehensive income or loss, which have been measured at fair value, and lease liabilities, which are measured at present value.  Key highlights Klarna delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of revenue above $1 billion and positive adjusted operating income. Transaction margin dollars grew 32%, and GMV rose 10% to $36.1 billion, led by 24% growth in the U.S. Fair Financing, our highest-earning product per dollar of volume, was also our fastest growing, up 61%. Adjusted operating income increased by $35 million year-over-year to $21 million. We now serve 122 million active consumers and 1.35 million merchants, the latter up 59%. Our strategy follows our business areas. Consumers typically discover Klarna through buy now, pay later in lifestyle spend, and from there we extend into everyday and big-ticket purchases with customers we have already underwritten. Underpinning all three, we also earn from consumer services and advertising: our shopping browser, agentic commerce and subscriptions. It generated $588 million of revenue in 2025 and has grown 30% so far this year. Over the past two years, Fair Financing has been our priority in the U.S. Volume reached $12.5 billion over the last 12 months, up 140% from $5.2 billion, supported by partners such as Walmart, through OnePay, Airbnb, and eBay. In Europe, our leadership in Pay Later and the strength of our brand give us a strong platform for Fair Financing, which reached $6.0 billion across our global ex-U.S. markets over the last 12 months, up 50%. Over a loan’s life, we target a transaction margin of 3% to 4% of volume on Fair Financing, more than three times what Pay Later earns per dollar of volume. The Klarna Card continued to scale, with third-quarter volume more than doubling to $4.5 billion. Subscriptions are becoming a meaningful source of high-value, recurring revenue: subscription revenue rose more than 500% to $43 million in the quarter. That is $178 million of annual recurring high margin revenue at September’s run rate. Card users shop with Klarna about three times as often, and the card is now used by 6% of our active consumers, rising to 11% in the U.S. During the quarter, we signed Fiserv, one of the largest U.S. payment processors, to offer Klarna to its merchants. Southwest Airlines and J.Crew launched Klarna in the U.S., and with Marks & Spencer now live, Klarna is available at every major UK department store. We also went live with Lands’ End, a classic American lifestyle brand, and CarParts.com, a leading U.S. online auto parts retailer. The Apple Upgrade program, launched in July, is gaining good traction as we approach our first holiday season together. Our shopping browser helps consumers discover products, compare and track prices, earn cashback and pay with Klarna. It has driven more than $34 billion of GMV since its launch in 2020. We are now building AI into this experience with our AI assistant, live with a small group of early users, with pre-registration open, on WhatsApp, iMessage and in the Klarna app. Heading into 2027, we see three key opportunities: scaling Fair Financing in the U.S. and expanding it across Europe, growing the Klarna Card beyond our merchant network, and AI to accelerate growth and productivity. 3 Klarna Q3’26 Earnings Release

 Our capital-light approach As a bank, Klarna benefits from a scalable funding base that supports continued growth. As of September 30, 2026, we had $12.7 billion of customer deposits, representing 88% of our total funding, and providing a stable and flexible funding base. This deposit base is a structural advantage: it lowers our funding costs and deepens our relationship with consumers. Our funding position is strong. Our model is designed to be low risk and highly capital efficient. Our products remain very short duration, and where duration grows, we can recycle capital because our risk profile is attractive to external capital providers. Klarna uses forward flows to recycle capital efficiently. Forward flows are committed, pre-priced loan sales, which reduce capital intensity, transfer credit exposure and accelerate revenue recognition. We are uniquely positioned to be able to use these instruments on our terms to deliver the best outcome for our shareholders.
